body: Knack II is Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 action-platform game, first released in North America on 5 September 2017. Knack and his companions investigate a threat connected to the High-Goblins and ancient weapons, with the hero's ability to change size shaping the journey. Combat, platforming and environmental puzzles sit beside a more developed set of attacks and upgrades. The sequel also makes cooperative play a central feature, allowing another person to join the story. A recognisable character becomes the basis for an adventure intended to be shared by players with different levels of experience.

Knack punches, kicks and deflects projectiles, while collected energy develops a skill tree and opens further possibilities. Changing size allows a space to be read differently, turning the body itself into one of the tools used to continue. Special forms such as Iron, Ice and Stealth alter both appearance and function. Treasure chests supply parts for additional upgrades, giving exploration another practical reward. The player learns when force is useful and when the next problem asks for a smaller shape or a particular ability, connecting development to the environment rather than only increasing damage.

A second local player can join or leave during the campaign, reducing the interruption involved in sharing the adventure. Takamitsu Iijima directed, Marianne Krawczyk and Mark Cerny wrote, and Anthony Willis composed the music. Reviews were mixed but generally regarded the sequel as an improvement on the original. Its cooperative structure gives the series a clearer social purpose. One player can help another through the same journey without requiring two separate campaigns or a strict commitment from the beginning, making the changing character's adventure something the people beside the television can enter together.
